scope: General JNI implemented-method metadata and real adopted Java Thread identity/lifetime, plus strengthened original SDK/NDK constructor proof; no application-specific behavior.

basis.implementation: Independent implementation of public JNI and implemented framework contracts; no JDK/ART implementation code copied.

observed_blocker.evidence: Actual JNI op2 records NoSuchMethodError for the exact descriptor, followed by op25 invalid token0. Earlier Thread FindClass now passes. This is startup diagnostic evidence, not game compatibility.
observed_blocker.prior_results: All three prior cases returned to launcher with matching installed identity; SD restored. Constructor proof stopped at String.getBytes(String), before its VFS result; encoding is a separately implemented contract.

implementation.catalog: FrameworkHost has an explicit default-none method metadata capability. Android advertises only implemented Thread/Executor overloads and kinds. JNI resolves real DEX definitions first, preserves actual declaring owner/static kind/native or abstract barriers, and does not inherit constructors. Lookup never executes a method body.
implementation.execution: Platform static IDs use the existing normal Engine static intrinsic/FrameworkHost execution path. Registered host constructors use existing initialized allocation/host attachment/constructor execution, with the actual receiver rooted before callbacks.
implementation.thread_identity: Thread.currentThread lazily adopts each real NativeHost thread identity as a genuine Java Thread. The exact bound application main owner receives main metadata; supplied modified-UTF8 JNI attach names are retained, otherwise a generated name is used. Existing executor worker identity wins, with fail-closed conflicting-owner rejection.
implementation.lifetime: Active adopted identities are roots. Real detach removes only the active owner mapping and marks the retained Java Thread terminated; external/global references keep observable name/id and isAlive false. Weak metadata is pruned when the object is collected; a reused native owner receives a new Java Thread. Adoption is separate from Timer/Executor callback-owner checks.
implementation.attachment: Explicit JNI attach validates supported JNI version, bounded4096-byte name and unsupported ThreadGroup before attachment succeeds. Rust registration occurs before C claims attachment success. Already-attached calls remain no-op. Platform runtime detach notifies framework under the existing VM lease after TLS callbacks.
implementation.bounds: Existing128 Thread object records and128 active named attachment metadata; exact owner0 and conflicting live identity fail closed. Constructor metadata is explicit; unknown classes/overloads receive no arbitrary callable method IDs.

The visible SDK Activity now independently asserts actual expected numeric/exception results before writing output.

limitations: This is a bounded implemented-method catalog, not complete Android method metadata or JNI compliance. Unknown APIs remain unavailable.
ThreadGroup attachment is rejected. JVM daemon process-exit policy, OS thread naming and full Java Thread/Looper/uncaught-handler semantics are not claimed.
The host owner-switching tests validate serialized VM semantics, not OS concurrency. Actual background/native pthread transport and retained references require the next NRO proof.
No game first screen or gameplay success is claimed; all new-source emulator and physical-device evidence remains separate.

A legacy executor test was updated to explicitly detach/re-attach a reused native owner and assert a fresh identity while the saved stopped Java Thread remains terminated. Earlier worker/TLS-owner assertions remain intact.
